name: Mishti Hub
dsc: Roshogolla is the crown jewel of Bengali sweets, featuring soft, spongy cottage cheese balls delicately soaked in a light sugar syrup that is perfectly balanced in sweetness. This classic tray includes 20 pieces, each crafted with precision to achieve that signature bounce and juicy texture. A beloved dessert across Bangladesh, roshogolla is an essential part of celebrations, family gatherings, and festive occasions like Pohela Boishakh and weddings.

name: Hilsa House
dsc: Ilish bhapa is a quintessential Bangladeshi dish where the national fish, hilsa, is steamed with mustard paste, green chilies, turmeric, and a drizzle of mustard oil. The steaming process locks in the fish's natural oils and flavors, creating a delicate yet pungent dish that is deeply satisfying. This iconic preparation is especially popular during the monsoon season and is traditionally served with steaming hot rice.

name: Bengal Kitchen
dsc: Khichuri is the ultimate Bangladeshi comfort food, made from rice and moong dal cooked together with turmeric, ginger, and a medley of spices until they reach a creamy, porridge-like consistency. This hearty one-pot meal is often prepared during rainy days, along with crispy fried eggplant, pickles, and fried onions. A staple in Bangladeshi households, khichuri evokes nostalgia and warmth with every spoonful.

name: Mishti Bhandar
dsc: Shondesh is a classic Bengali sweet made from fresh chhena and sugar, delicately flavored with cardamom and often garnished with pistachio slivers. This premium box contains 16 pieces of this melt-in-your-mouth delicacy, each carefully shaped into intricate designs. A favorite during weddings, Pohela Boishakh, and Durga Puja, shondesh is the perfect gift for sweet lovers across Bangladesh.

name: Machh Bhaja
dsc: Chitol maach muitha is a quintessential Bangladeshi delicacy where fish balls made from chitol fish are simmered in a rich, spicy gravy. The fish is carefully deboned, mixed with aromatic spices, and shaped into dumplings before being cooked in a tomato and onion-based sauce. This labor-intensive dish is reserved for special occasions, showcasing the culinary expertise of Bangladeshi kitchens and grandmothers' secret recipes.

name: Spice House
dsc: Kala bhuna is a legendary Bangladeshi beef dish famous for its deep, dark color achieved through slow-cooking with a medley of roasted spices. The beef is cooked until tender and infused with flavors of cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves, resulting in a rich, aromatic gravy. A staple at weddings, Eid celebrations, and special gatherings, kala bhuna is best enjoyed with fragrant pulao or paratha.

name: Fisherman's Delight
dsc: Doi maach is a classic Bengali fish curry where pieces of rui or katla fish are cooked in a creamy, yogurt-based gravy infused with ginger, garlic, and a hint of mustard oil. This dish perfectly balances tanginess from the yogurt with the warmth of spices, creating a rich and comforting meal. Traditionally served with steamed rice, it is a favorite in Bangladeshi households during weekends and celebrations.

name: Pulao House
dsc: Misti pulao is a fragrant and slightly sweet rice dish made from premium gobindobhog rice, cooked with ghee, sugar, and whole spices like cinnamon and cardamom, then garnished with raisins and cashews. This delightful pulao is a must-have during weddings and celebrations, pairing beautifully with spicy curries or bhuna meat. Each bite offers a perfect balance of sweetness and aromatic spices.

name: Poultry Chef
dsc: Bhuna murgi is a dry, intensely flavorful chicken dish where the meat is slow-cooked with onions, ginger, garlic, and a robust blend of spices until it is tender and coated in a rich, thick masala. The slow-cooking process allows the flavors to deeply penetrate the meat, creating a dish that is aromatic and incredibly satisfying. Perfect for pairing with paratha, naan, or simple steamed rice.

name: Sweet Corner
dsc: Patisapta is a traditional Bengali sweet pancake made from flour and semolina batter, stuffed with a luscious filling of coconut and jaggery, and folded into delicate rolls. These sweet rolls are then drizzled with a light sugar syrup, adding an extra layer of sweetness. A winter favorite in Bangladesh, patisapta is often prepared during Poush Parbon, a harvest festival celebrating the new crop with traditional pithas.

name: Hilsa Heritage
dsc: Shorshe ilish is the crown jewel of Bangladeshi cuisine, featuring the national fish, hilsa, cooked in a pungent and flavorful mustard seed paste with green chilies and turmeric. The rich, oily texture of the hilsa blends beautifully with the sharpness of mustard, creating a dish that is cherished across the country. This iconic dish is an emotion for every Bangladeshi, especially during the monsoon season when hilsa is at its best.

name: Tehari House
dsc: Tehari is a fragrant rice dish made with caramelized onions, aromatic spices, and succulent pieces of beef or mutton, all cooked together to create a harmonious blend of flavors. Unlike biryani, tehari has a lighter, more subtle taste with a distinct caramelized onion flavor. A staple at Eid celebrations, Bangladeshi weddings, and family gatherings, tehari is traditionally served with raita, salad, and boiled eggs.

name: Coconut Bliss
dsc: Narkel naru is a beloved Bengali sweet made from fresh grated coconut and jaggery, cooked together until they form a thick, sticky mixture that is then shaped into small, bite-sized balls. Sometimes flavored with cardamom or dry ginger, these little treats are a must-have during Lakshmi Puja and other religious ceremonies. Each naru offers a delightful chewiness and natural sweetness from the jaggery.

name: Bhorta Bari
dsc: Dal bhorta is a simple yet flavorful Bangladeshi side dish where roasted red lentils are mashed with mustard oil, green chilies, onions, and fresh cilantro. This humble preparation packs a punch with its bold, earthy flavors and is a staple in most Bangladeshi meals. Served alongside rice, dal bhorta is a comforting dish that brings back nostalgic memories of home-cooked meals and grandmother's kitchen.

name: Tea Time Snacks
dsc: Jhuri bhaja is a crispy, savory snack made from thin strips of potatoes, sweet potatoes, or vegetables that are deep-fried until golden and crunchy. Sprinkled with salt, chili powder, and chaat masala, this snack is a favorite during monsoon evenings and tea time gatherings. The light, airy texture and addictive flavor make jhuri bhaja a popular street food and homemade treat across Bangladesh.

name: Sweet Shop BD
dsc: Pantua is a classic Bengali sweet similar to gulab jamun but darker and slightly denser, made from khoya and flour, deep-fried to perfection, and soaked in a fragrant sugar syrup. These golden-brown balls are infused with cardamom and rose water for an aromatic finish. A favorite during Durga Puja, Eid, and festive celebrations, pantua is a sweet that transcends generations in Bangladesh.

name: Spice Kitchen
dsc: Murgi mangsho is the ultimate Bangladeshi chicken curry, cooked with potatoes, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a blend of aromatic spices that create a rich, flavorful gravy. The slow-cooking process ensures the meat is tender and falls off the bone, while the potatoes soak up all the delicious flavors. This quintessential dish is served with rice, pulao, or roti for a satisfying family meal.

name: Mishti Doi Hub
dsc: Mishti doi is a sweetened, caramelized yogurt that is a cherished dessert in Bangladesh and West Bengal. Made by fermenting milk with sugar and jaggery in clay pots, mishti doi has a creamy, velvety texture and a distinct sweet-sour flavor. This jar contains 500g of this iconic dessert, often enjoyed as the perfect ending to a traditional Bengali meal or festive celebration.

name: Rezala House
dsc: Chicken rezala is a flavorful, mildly spicy curry with Mughlai origins, made with chicken, yogurt, and a rich blend of ground spices including cardamom, cinnamon, and mace. The dish has a distinctive white or pale yellow color and a creamy, aromatic gravy that is perfect for soaking up with naan or pulao. A favorite for weddings and special occasions across Bangladesh, rezala is a true royal treat.

name: Snack Corner
dsc: Shingara is the Bangladeshi version of the samosa, featuring a crispy, flaky pastry filled with a savory mixture of spiced potatoes, peas, and sometimes minced meat. The triangular pastries are deep-fried until golden and serve as the perfect tea-time snack. This party pack includes 24 pieces of these beloved snacks, guaranteed to be a hit at any gathering, celebration, or rainy afternoon.

name: Beef House
dsc: Beef vuna is a classic Bangladeshi dish where tender beef is slow-cooked with caramelized onions, ginger, garlic, and a rich blend of whole and ground spices. The dish is cooked until the gravy thickens and coats the meat, resulting in a deeply flavorful, aromatic preparation. This favorite Eid dish is traditionally served with tehari, pulao, or flaky parathas for an indulgent family feast.

name: Kodom Sweet
dsc: Kheer kodom is a unique Bengali sweet shaped like the kodom flower, made from a blend of flour, khoya, and sugar, deep-fried to a crispy texture, and soaked in thickened milk. This sweet is known for its rich, layered texture and aromatic flavor, often enjoyed during religious festivals and special celebrations. The artistic shape and delightful taste make it a treasured sweet in every Bangladeshi household.

name: Street Food BD
dsc: Muri telebhaja is the quintessential Bangladeshi street food combo featuring puffed rice mixed with a variety of crispy deep-fried snacks like dal puri, vegetable fritters, and spicy potatoes. This platter includes a generous serving of muri paired with freshly made telebhaja, ready to be enjoyed with a sprinkle of chili powder and a squeeze of lemon. Perfect for a quick, satisfying bite on any busy day.

name: Pitha Ghar
dsc: Pitha utsav platter brings together the best of Bangladeshi pithas, including bhapa pitha, patisapta, puli pitha, and other traditional varieties, served with a variety of sweet and savory accompaniments. This generous platter features 20 assorted pithas, each carefully prepared using traditional recipes passed down through generations. A winter favorite, pithas are an integral part of Poush Sankranti celebrations, showcasing Bangladesh's rich culinary heritage.

name: Mishti Market
dsc: Chomchom is a traditional Bengali sweet made from fresh chhena, shaped into elongated or cylindrical pieces, and soaked in a light sugar syrup. These soft, spongy treats are often delicately flavored with cardamom or rose water and garnished with coconut or mawa. Known for their unique texture and delightful sweetness, chomchom is a beloved dessert for celebrations and festive occasions in every region of Bangladesh.

name: Rural Kitchen
dsc: Sorisha ga tehari is a rustic twist on the classic Bangladeshi tehari, where mustard seeds are ground into a paste and added to the rice along with caramelized onions and spices. The result is a fragrant, slightly pungent rice dish that is hearty and deeply satisfying, featuring generous pieces of beef or goat meat. This traditional preparation is popular in rural areas of Bangladesh, especially during cold winter evenings.

name: Old Dhaka Delight
dsc: Bakarkhani is a traditional, flaky flatbread with a rich history in Dhaka, made from flour, ghee, sugar, and aromatic spices like cardamom and poppy seeds. Baked until golden and crisp, this bread has a unique sweet-salty flavor and a layered texture reminiscent of puff pastry. A popular item during Mughal times, it remains a favorite for breakfast or as a tea-time snack in Old Dhaka.

name: Bhuna House
dsc: Mutton kala bhuna takes the classic beef preparation to the next level, featuring tender pieces of mutton cooked in a dark, intensely flavored gravy made from a secret blend of roasted spices. This legendary dish from Chittagong is the result of hours of slow cooking, where the meat absorbs all the complex flavors, creating a rich, satisfying meal. Served with plain rice or paratha, it's a true delicacy.

name: Summer Treats
dsc: Amras rosh is a sweet, thick mango pulp made from ripe mangoes, sugar, and cardamom, traditionally enjoyed during the summer months in Bangladesh. This bowl contains a generous serving of the pulp, often paired with flatbreads like luchi or puri for a satisfying meal. A popular dessert during the mango season, amras rosh captures the essence of summer with its rich, fruity flavor and golden color.

name: Chanachur Corner
dsc: Ful bari chanachur is the ultimate Bengali snack mix, featuring a delightful combination of crispy fried noodles, peanuts, dried peas, and a variety of crunchy ingredients, all tossed with a savory spice mix. This jar contains 500g of this addictive snack, perfect for tea-time gatherings, long train journeys, or simply as a pick-me-up during a busy day. A must-have in every Bangladeshi household for guests.

name: Pitha Palace
dsc: Taler pitha is a traditional Bengali winter cake made from date palm jaggery and rice flour, steamed or fried to perfection. These cakes are known for their distinct sweet, earthy flavor from the jaggery and have a soft, chewy texture that is deeply satisfying. This box contains 16 pieces of this seasonal delight, bringing the warmth and sweetness of Bangladesh's winter harvest directly to your table.

name: Polao House
dsc: Murgi polao is a festive rice dish where fragrant gobindobhog rice is cooked with chicken, ghee, and a blend of aromatic spices like cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. The chicken is partially cooked with the rice, allowing its flavors to infuse every grain. This special dish is a staple at Bengali weddings, Eid celebrations, and family get-togethers, served with a side of creamy raita and crispy salad.

name: Shutki House
dsc: Shutki bhorta is a traditional Bangladeshi dish made from dried fish, mashed with mustard oil, green chilies, onions, and fresh cilantro. The pungent, intense flavor of dried fish combined with the sharpness of mustard oil creates a bold, earthy taste that is cherished by many. This dish is particularly popular in the coastal regions of Bangladesh and is served as a side with steaming hot rice.

name: Biryani House
dsc: Kacchi biryani is one of Bangladesh's most beloved dishes, featuring raw marinated mutton layered with partially cooked rice, sealed in a pot, and slow-cooked over dum (steam). The meat becomes incredibly tender while the rice absorbs all the juices and aromatic spices, creating a symphony of flavors. A must-have at weddings, celebrations, and Eid feasts, this biryani is a true masterpiece of Bangladeshi cuisine.

name: Luchi Ghar
dsc: Luchi alur dom is a classic Bengali breakfast or brunch combination featuring deep-fried, puffy flatbreads served alongside a flavorful, mildly spiced potato curry. The luchis are light and airy, made from refined flour, while the alur dom is a rich curry with potatoes cooked in a tomato-based gravy with ginger, garlic, and aromatic spices. This iconic pair is a weekend favorite in Bangladeshi homes.

name: Sour Fish
dsc: Chitol machher tok is a unique Bengali fish curry with a tangy twist, where pieces of chitol fish are cooked in a tamarind-based sour gravy with ginger, garlic, and green chilies. The tartness of the tamarind balances beautifully with the richness of the fish, creating a light, refreshing dish that is especially popular in summer. This traditional preparation is enjoyed with plain steamed rice.

name: Gur Sweet
dsc: Gur murki is a traditional Bangladeshi sweet made from date palm jaggery and puffed rice, combined and shaped into bite-sized balls or bars. The rich, caramel-like flavor of the jaggery pairs perfectly with the light, crunchy texture of the puffed rice, creating a delightful treat that is both satisfying and nutritious. A popular winter snack, gur murki is a favorite during the harvest season and festive celebrations.

name: Bhorta Platter
dsc: Bangladeshi bhorta platter brings together a variety of mashed side dishes including shutki bhorta, dal bhorta, alu bhorta (mashed potato), and begun bhorta (roasted eggplant mash), each prepared with mustard oil, green chilies, and fresh herbs. This platter includes generous portions of each bhorta, accompanied by fresh salad and lemon wedges. An essential part of a traditional Bengali meal, bhortas add depth and character.

name: Sweet Snack
dsc: Handesh is a traditional Bengali sweet snack made from rice flour and jaggery, deep-fried into small, golden-brown discs that are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. This simple yet delicious treat is often prepared during Poush Parbon and other festive occasions, served as a tea-time snack or dessert. The caramelized jaggery flavor gives handesh its unique sweetness and rustic charm.

name: Pitha Season
dsc: Notun gur pitha is a Bengali winter delicacy made with freshly harvested date palm jaggery and rice flour, steamed or fried into soft, sweet cakes. The use of new jaggery (notun gur) gives these pithas a distinctive, earthy sweetness that is unlike any other sweetener. This box contains 12 pieces of these seasonal treats, celebrating the arrival of winter and the harvest season in Bangladesh.
